findings.title: Builder cannot consume subsequent explicitly trusted scopes
findings.observed: bound_roots compares both an absolute cp570 scope pathname and a compiled-in SHA. An identical-byte copy (same trusted SHA) under reviewer root is rejected; a new scope with new artifact/receipt roots is also rejected. CLI has only --scope, no trusted-scope digest/provider input. Internal authorized_roots argument bypass exists only in Python calls/tests and is not a scoped authenticated CLI entry.
findings.impact: The reusable builder is tied to this machine and temporary review scope. New authorized build scopes require editing production builder source, and removing/moving historical receipt cp570 breaks the CLI. Scope pinning should bind invocation authority rather than permanent construction history.
findings.minimal_fix: Accept a new explicit trusted scope binding from the authorized caller (for example --scope plus out-of-band expected --scope-sha256); compare exact raw bytes before consuming roots. Validate required scope contract/worktree/root fields and continue canonical/reparse/direct-child/non-overlap/create-new checks. Do not treat a self-computed digest or arbitrary roots alone as authorization. The exact frozen source marker/product provenance may remain pinned as required by P1a.
